_about: Aesthetic policy for lib/visual.mjs, not architecture: every table here may be replaced. moodThreshold: how far (in axis units) a song's mean axes must lean along an overlay's direction before it has that mood; an overlay vector is ~.3-.5 long. selection: how a song with no `visual` header picks its world, deliberately fuzzy: each world's row is a base score plus weights over the song's features (every axis by name as its mean lean in -1..1, and tempo, sections, repetition, complexity, melody, pad from featuresOf), the scores go through a softmax at `temperature` (higher: more even odds), and the song's seed samples from the odds, so a world that fits moderately can still win and the same song always gets the same world. temperature: key mode -> a palette word. palette: visual property -> the axis whose song-wide mean it reads. voices: drum voice -> its role in any world. kinds: layer kind -> the slots it may take, in order; grain is unbounded and every list ends there. worlds: slot capacities per world. compositions: the director's presets, count the worlds each takes when the song lists none (filled from the selection's odds). defaultComposition: the preset a song with no `visual.composition` plays (single for the bare world).

single.about: one world full-frame: the stage as it always was

overlay.about: the primary full; the second world breathing in and out over it every eight bars, up to a peak the section's energy sets

tunnel.about: A wall of rings rushing at the camera at the tempo: the beat you can see coming, and it reads from across the room.

ink.about: The song paints one sheet and the last frame is the painting: the whole arrangement at a glance.

sediment.about: The song as rock strata rising through the frame: the sections stack into a record you can read.

signal.about: An instrumented panel, always moving and never accumulating: every part a node on a schematic.

swarm.about: One flock streaming after the melody: mass and flow rather than separate hits.

orrery.about: A celestial system: the bass is the gravity and every line part a body in orbit.

loom.about: A weaving machine making cloth: each part drives a mechanism and leaves its row behind.

growth.about: One organism grown tip by tip: the whole song's history standing as a plant.

rave.about: The stage seen over a crowd of sock monkeys: built for a loud section.

combo.about: A small band in a ring, each body the instrument it plays: best where parts trade the lead.

train.about: The view out a train window, a landscape per section: for long songs that travel.

parlor.about: The common room of an old folks' home, every part a resident: the humour is the point.

outrun.about: A 1995 arcade racer driven by the music: a stage per section, a checkpoint at every boundary.

cabaret.about: One old performer alone on a proscenium: for a song with a clear lead part.

dish.about: A petri dish under a microscope, a species per part: dense hats and rare hits both read.

faces.about: Portraits, one face close up hat to collar, cutting on the snare.

tableau.about: A fashion-editorial video: twenty-four recurring actors on three sets, cutting with the arrangement.

undead.about: A night-street dance video after Thriller: a lead in a red jacket, the dead rising in rows behind, one step a beat.

thriller.about: The tableau's cast and poses swapped for zombies in 80s clothes doing the Thriller choreography; the sets, the cutting and the dance stay.
